senses.definition: Very unpleasant to look at, hear, or think about.
senses.example: The scratched wall had an ugly green stain.

senses.definition: A group of flowers with stalks that spread from near one spot, like ribs of an umbrella.
senses.example: The small flower stalks in Queen Anne's lace make an umbel.

senses.definition: A folding cover held up on a handle to keep rain or sunlight off a person.
senses.example: Three of us crowded under one big umbrella.

senses.definition: Not, or the opposite of. It can describe someone or something that lacks a quality.
senses.example: In the word unfair, un- means not fair.

senses.definition: To reverse an action or take something away.
senses.example: In untie, un- shows that you undo the knot.

senses.definition: Not knowing or noticing that something is happening or true.
senses.example: I was unaware that my jacket was inside out.

senses.definition: So difficult, unpleasant, or painful that you feel you cannot put up with it.
senses.example: The heat in the kitchen felt unbearable while the bread baked.

senses.definition: Not sure or not known for certain.
senses.example: We were uncertain about which door led to the gym.

senses.definition: A brother of one of your parents, or the husband of your aunt or uncle.
senses.example: My uncle taught me how to make pancakes.

senses.definition: To remove a cover from something or find something that was hidden.
senses.example: We uncovered a painted sign under the old paper.

senses.definition: Not yet having made a choice.
senses.example: I was still undecided about which book to take on the trip.

senses.definition: Lower than or directly below something.
senses.example: Our dog slept under the porch.

senses.definition: Less than a number or amount.
senses.example: Children under ten needed an adult with them.

senses.definition: Controlled, affected, or guided by something.
senses.example: The library was under repair for a week.

senses.definition: Feeling a little sick or unwell.
senses.example: I felt under the weather, so I rested on the couch.

senses.definition: To think something is smaller, easier, or less important than it really is.
senses.example: I underestimated how many boxes would be needed for all those books.

senses.definition: Located or happening below the ground.
senses.example: An underground pipe carried water to the house.

senses.definition: Under the surface of the ground.
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared underground.

senses.definition: In a lower place with something above or covering it.
senses.example: The missing button was underneath the rug.

senses.definition: In a lower or covered part.
senses.example: The loaf looked done on top but was still pale underneath.

senses.definition: A road or path that goes below another road or railroad so they can cross at different levels.
senses.example: We walked through the underpass to reach the field.

senses.definition: To know what something means, how it works, or why it happened.
senses.example: I understood the directions after seeing someone try the first step.

senses.definition: To agree or decide to start an important piece of work.
senses.example: Our class will undertake the job of cleaning the old garden.

senses.definition: Below the surface of water.
senses.example: An underwater camera photographed the plants.

senses.definition: In a place below the surface of water.
senses.example: I listened to the muffled tapping while I was underwater.

senses.definition: Clothing worn next to the body under other clothes.
senses.example: I packed clean underwear for each day of camp.

senses.definition: To reverse an action, such as opening something that was fastened or taking back a change.
senses.example: I undid the knot and put the rope away.

senses.definition: To cancel the most recent change in a computer program.
senses.example: I clicked undo after moving the wrong picture.

senses.definition: A little worried or uncomfortable about what might happen.
senses.example: I felt uneasy when I heard footsteps in the empty hall.

senses.definition: Not flat, smooth, level, or equal all the way across.
senses.example: We stepped carefully over the uneven stones.

senses.definition: Treating some people worse than others without a good reason, or going against agreed rules.
senses.example: It felt unfair to change the rules after the game started.

senses.definition: Not known to you because you have not seen, heard, or used it enough.
senses.example: I checked the map whenever I reached an unfamiliar street.

senses.definition: To open something that has been folded.
senses.example: We unfolded the map on the table.

senses.definition: To happen or become clear in a series of events.
senses.example: We listened as the story unfolded.

senses.definition: Not welcoming, helpful, or kind.
senses.example: The character’s first reply sounded unfriendly, but she soon invited us inside.

senses.definition: Sad or dissatisfied with something.
senses.example: The puppy looked unhappy when its favorite toy rolled under the couch.

senses.definition: A shared set of numbers that stand for text characters people use around the world.
senses.example: Unicode helps different phones agree on which letter to show.

senses.definition: Clothing that members of a group wear to show they belong to it.
senses.example: Each player wore a green uniform with a white number.

senses.definition: Staying the same over a whole area or group.
senses.example: We rolled the dough to a uniform thickness.

senses.definition: Happening even though no one meant for it to happen.
senses.example: Knocking over the second domino was an unintended result of moving the first.

senses.definition: A joining together of groups or things into a whole, or the group that is formed.
senses.example: The two small clubs formed a union to look after the field.

senses.definition: An organization of workers who act together on matters such as pay and working conditions.
senses.example: The workers asked their union to help them plan a meeting.

senses.definition: The only one of its kind, or very different from others in an important way.
senses.example: Each club member painted a unique design on their kite.

senses.definition: One thing used for counting or measuring.
senses.example: To measure the rope, we chose the meter as our unit.

senses.definition: One part of a course that studies related ideas.
senses.example: Our first science unit covered plants.

senses.definition: A comparison that gives the amount of one thing for one unit of another.
senses.example: Six eggs for three dollars gives a unit rate of two eggs per dollar.

senses.definition: To join people or things together for the same purpose or in one group.
senses.example: The teams united to clean up the field after the big game.

senses.definition: Applying to everyone or present everywhere in a given group or place.
senses.example: The dislike of soggy shoes seemed almost universal among the hikers.

senses.definition: All of space and time and everything in them, including Earth, stars, and galaxies.
senses.example: We can see only part of the universe from Earth.

senses.definition: Not yet identified or learned about.
senses.example: The artist who painted the old sign is unknown.

senses.definition: A fact or amount that has yet to be found.
senses.example: In our math problem, the unknown was the number of marbles in the bag.

senses.definition: Except if something else is true or happens.
senses.example: We will play outside unless it rains.

senses.definition: Not expected to happen or probably not true.
senses.example: It seems unlikely that the ice will last through this warm afternoon.

senses.definition: Having no fixed limit in amount or number.
senses.example: The site allowed an unlimited number of practice rounds.

senses.definition: To take things out of or off a vehicle, package, or container that was carrying them.
senses.example: We helped unload books from the library van.

senses.definition: To open or release something held by a lock, or to make a protected part available.
senses.example: I entered the password to unlock the tablet.

senses.definition: To take things out of a suitcase, box, or other container.
senses.example: We unpacked the games after we arrived.

senses.definition: To explain a complicated idea by looking closely at its smaller parts.
senses.example: Our teacher helped us unpack the meaning of the final line.

senses.definition: Not enjoyable, comfortable, or nice.
senses.example: A loud rattle made the bus ride unpleasant.

senses.definition: To pull the plug of a device out of the place where it connects to power or another device.
senses.example: Dad unplugged the old clock so he could move it to the shelf.

senses.definition: To open something that was rolled up so it lies flat or spread out.
senses.example: We unrolled the long map across two desks.

senses.definition: To separate things that are twisted or knotted together.
senses.example: I untangled a length of jump rope from the handle.

senses.definition: To open or loosen a knot or something held by a knot.
senses.example: I untied the ribbon without tearing the paper.

senses.definition: Up to the time named.
senses.example: The library is open until five.

senses.definition: Continuing up to the time when something happens.
senses.example: We waited under the shelter until the rain stopped.

senses.definition: Different from what is common or expected.
senses.example: It was unusual to see snow so late in spring.

senses.definition: Not feeling healthy or well.
senses.example: The actor who was unwell stayed home, so another student read the part.

senses.definition: Toward a higher place or level.
senses.example: Look up at the notice on the wall.

senses.definition: Toward a higher part or farther along something.
senses.example: We walked up the hill to see the view.

senses.definition: Awake, or out of bed after resting.
senses.example: I was up early enough to watch the sunrise.

senses.definition: Cheerful, hopeful, or lively.
senses.example: Everyone felt upbeat after hearing the new song.

senses.definition: Planned or expected to happen soon.
senses.example: We painted a sign for the upcoming book fair.

senses.definition: A newer form of software that can make changes or fix problems.
senses.example: An update fixed the app that kept closing.

senses.definition: A change that makes something better or adds useful features.
senses.example: Lights were an upgrade for the old bike.

senses.definition: To improve something or replace it with a more useful version.
senses.example: We upgraded the model car by putting larger wheels on it.

senses.definition: On, or soon after something happens.
senses.example: Upon reaching the lake, we stopped to eat lunch.

senses.definition: Higher than another part or closer to the top.
senses.example: The book was on the upper shelf.

senses.definition: Standing with the bottom down and the top up, rather than lying flat or leaning.
senses.example: Keep the tub upright so the water stays inside.

senses.definition: Worried, sad, or angry about something.
senses.example: I was upset when I lost my favorite hat.

senses.definition: To make someone feel worried, sad, or angry.
senses.example: The bad news upset the whole team.

senses.definition: To knock a thing over or disturb how it normally works.
senses.example: Do not upset the bowl while you carry the tray.

senses.definition: With the top where the bottom usually is, or turned over completely.
senses.example: We put the cups upside down on the drying mat.

senses.definition: Up a set of stairs or on a floor above this one.
senses.example: I ran upstairs to get my notebook.

senses.definition: Going or pointing toward a higher place.
senses.example: The bird made an upward turn past the treetops.

senses.definition: Toward a higher place or position.
senses.example: I looked upward at the top of the climbing wall.

senses.definition: Having to do with a city or a densely built area.
senses.example: A small garden gave the urban neighborhood a green space.

senses.definition: A part of a city that is warmer than nearby areas with fewer streets or buildings and more plants.
senses.example: Our street had a stronger urban heat island before the new trees grew.

senses.definition: To try hard to make someone do or consider something by asking or encouraging them.
senses.example: The librarian urged us to read the book’s surprising last chapter.

senses.definition: A strong feeling of wanting to do something.
senses.example: I had an urge to laugh when the actor forgot his hat.

senses.definition: Needing attention very soon or right away.
senses.example: The message was urgent, so I took it straight to the office.

senses.definition: The liquid waste you pass when you pee.
senses.example: The kidneys make urine and send it to the bladder.

senses.definition: A web address that tells a browser how and where to ask for something.
senses.example: The URL leads to a different page on the same site.

senses.definition: A way something serves a purpose.
senses.example: We found a new use for the empty jar.

senses.definition: To do something with a tool, material, or idea for a particular purpose.
senses.example: Use the ruler to mark a straight edge.

senses.definition: To consume or take part of an amount that is available.
senses.example: We used nearly all the paint on the first sign.

senses.definition: Helping you do something or solve a problem.
senses.example: A pocket map was useful when our phone ran out of power.

senses.definition: Unable to help or be used for what you need.
senses.example: The torn map was useless because our route was on the missing part.

senses.definition: Happening or done in the way that is most common or expected.
senses.example: We met at our usual table by the window.

senses.definition: A tool you use for a task, especially for cooking, serving, or eating.
senses.example: I looked for a kitchen utensil that could turn the pancake.
